The Indus River. One of the world's major rivers, flowing approximately thirty-one hundred eighty kilometers from the Tibetan Plateau westward through India and Pakistan to the Arabian Sea. It is the lifeline of Pakistan's agriculture and economy, and is shared by India and Pakistan under the nineteen sixty Indus Waters Treaty, one of the world's most successful international water-sharing agreements.

The Indus originates in the Tibetan Plateau and flows southwest through the Himalayas, then across the Thar Desert and the Pakistani plains. The Indus Valley Civilization, dating from roughly twenty-six hundred to nineteen hundred before the Common Era, was one of the world's earliest urban cultures, with cities like Harappa and Mohenjo-daro. The Indus Delta in Pakistan is shrinking due to upstream dams blocking sediment flow and rising sea levels from climate change.

The Indus Waters Treaty of nineteen sixty divides the river's waters between India and Pakistan, representing a landmark example of international cooperation over shared resources. Major cities along the river include Lahore, Multan, and Hyderabad, centers of Mughal and Islamic culture. Water diversion through irrigation systems has reduced the lower delta's flow so that the river now rarely reaches the sea with significant volume. The river is sacred in Sikhism and Hinduism, and Indus dolphins are endemic freshwater cetaceans found nowhere else on Earth.
